speaker_role: independent counselor (head of counseling at Insight Education, per self-introduction)
commercial_incentive: mild self-promotion: plugs the company's blog list of schools that track demonstrated interest and its alumni mentor network
key_insights: Demonstrated interest as a formal, trackable admissions signal is described as having emerged roughly five to six years before the video was made
Colleges use it partly to protect yield by favoring applicants likely to actually enroll if admitted

Large public universities generally do not weigh demonstrated interest since applicant volume makes it infeasible to track; it matters more for smaller, lesser-known, or liberal arts colleges avoiding over-admitting
Virtual engagement (info sessions, tours, chats with current students) counts the same as in-person visits and expanded greatly, leveling the playing field for students who cannot travel
College CRM systems track email opens and link clicks, so promptly engaging with recruitment emails is itself a measurable interest signal

Recommends researching a school before an info session and asking specific questions (e.g., about campus stress culture) rather than generic ones easily found online, both for better information and to stand out
notable_or_distinctive: explicitly frames demonstrated interest as mattering mainly for smaller/lesser-known colleges and losing relevance at increasingly popular big publics, a segmentation spelled out more clearly here than elsewhere in this batch
reliability_notes: counselor's claims (e.g., the '5-6 years old' origin, which schools track it) are asserted without citation; otherwise fairly grounded and not heavily sales-driven
